rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's administrative-assistance provision. Its section 3 and the child's section 5 share an unusually close sequence and wording: agencies identified through section 1 must furnish assistance under section 214 of the May 3, 1945 act, and that assistance may include detailed employees, one serving as executive officer, who perform functions assigned by the body consistent with the order's purposes. C01 contains nearly the same machinery and is a strong alternative, while C13 repeats it with an executive secretary rather than executive officer. The exact correspondence goes beyond generic committee boilerplate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The agencies designated in section 1 of this order shall, as may be necessary for the purpose of effectuating the provisions of this order, furnish assistance to the Committee in accordance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each executive department the head of which is referred to in section 1 of this order shall, as may be necessary for the purpose of effectuating the provisions of this order, furnish assistance to the Council in accordance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945...
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reproduces the parent provision's syntax, statutory authority, cross-reference to section 1, and assistance mechanism, changing primarily the designated body.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such assistance may include detailing employees to the Committee, one of whom may serve as its executive officer, to perform such functions consistent with the purpose of this order as the Committee may assign to them.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Such assistance may include detailing employees to the Council, one of whom may serve as its executive officer, to perform such functions consistent with the purposes of this order as the Council may assign to them.
shared_material.explanation: This is an almost verbatim transfer of a detailed staffing mechanism, including the executive-officer role and assignment of functions.
